articles.title: 包裹在途实时可视可管：中国移动 × 无锡邮政 × 华为完成物流领域首个广域蜂窝无源物联场景化验证
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，据华为无线网络官方公众号分享，2026 世界物联网博览会期间，中国移动江苏公司无锡分公司联合无锡邮政、华为完成物流领域首个广域蜂窝无源物联场景化验证。据介绍，以往邮袋信息化管理缺位、逆向回收困难，难以实时掌握在途位置与状态，末端回收率低。三方此次联合从邮袋追踪这一刚需场景切入，在真实支线运输中打通“标签 — 基站 — 核心网 — 平台”端到端全链路，实现邮政包裹在途全程实时可视可管。IT之家注：邮袋是邮件容器的一种，一般用帆布制作。是邮件在分拣封发和运输中最常使用的一种邮件容器。邮袋有多种型号和规格，包括普通款、方底款、拉链款等，以及国内特快邮袋、国际水陆路邮袋等类型。在无锡样板点中，中国移动 × 无锡邮政 × 华为实现小区连片组网，覆盖长三角邮件集散中心至硕放揽投部全程路段。另外，通过广域蜂窝无源物联标签的应用，邮政包裹可自动与基站建立连接，经核心网汇聚后统一接入可视化追踪平台，实现邮袋的在途位置与状态实时可查。IT之家注意到，广域蜂窝无源物联技术还具备免电池、易部署、广联接、低成本等优势 —— 标签即贴即用，通过蜂窝网络即可接入，赋能哑设备实现“应联尽联”；可视化平台统一管理，可支撑邮袋常态化运维，为可复制、可推广的智慧物流方案奠定基础。▲ 广域蜂窝无源物联标签目前，广域蜂窝无源物联的标准化工作已在 3GPP R20 中立项推进，预计 2027 年上半年标准冻结。

articles.title: 任天堂社长古川俊太郎称 Switch 2 游戏机暂无进一步涨价计划
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，任天堂在 2027 财年半年报披露，公司二季度（即 7 月至 9 月）共出货 267 万台 Switch 2 游戏机，较去年同期的 454 万台下降 41%。受内存短缺潮影响，任天堂已在今年 5 月（日本）/9 月（北美、欧洲等地）上调 Switch 2 售价。不过根据 IGN 报道，任天堂社长古川俊太郎坚持表示，公司拥有足够的内存供应，能够满足截至 2027 年 3 月销售 1650 万台 Switch 2 目标，当前没有进一步调整售价的考虑。同时，Switch 2 的累计销量已经来到 2635 万台。如果按照上市后的同期表现进行比较，Switch 2 是领先于初代 Switch 的。外界预计，任天堂将在 2027 年为 Switch 2 推出多款重磅游戏，其中包含粉丝期待已久的下一款正统马力欧续作。《宝可梦风》和《宝可梦波》已确认将于明年推出。

articles.title: 苹果 iOS 27.3 代码暗示，HomeView 有望支持 ChatGPT、Claude 等第三方 AI 应用
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，代码显示，苹果计划在 iOS 27.3 测试版中为 HomeView 增加对 ChatGPT、Claude 等第三方 AI 聊天机器人的支持。IT之家注意到，本月初，爆料者 pdfu 发现系统中存在一个尚未启用的 ConversationalApps 标记，因此推测 ChatGPT、Claude 等 AI 应用可能会接入 HomeView。如今，该爆料者表示，iOS 27.3 测试版中的代码已经证实了这一猜测。pdfu 写道：“这件事真的要来了，各位：AI 应用即将登陆 HomeView。作为 HomeView 车载互联桥接工具的 PebblePlay，已在 iOS 27.3 中获得 Conversational Apps（对话类应用）类别。”苹果通过这类标记来决定设备允许运行哪些类别的第三方应用，其运作方式与 CarPlay 类似。此外，该爆料者近期还发现了另一项代码线索，显示 HomeView 未来可能兼作 HomeKit 安全摄像头。HomeView 是苹果于 2026 年 10 月 13 日正式推出的首款智能家居中枢设备，定位为家庭共用的智能显示屏，集智能家居控制、音乐播放、视频通话和家庭监控等功能于一体。

articles.title: OPPO 面向 6G 时代重要技术布局，全球首个端网智能体意图通信白皮书发布
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，中国移动全球合作伙伴大会今日在广州开幕。OPPO 官方宣布，其携折叠旗舰、影像旗舰、AI、山海通信及 6G 通信等产品与技术参展，并发布全球首个端网智能体意图通信白皮书。OPPO 官方表示，在 6G 从“连接增强”走向“智能原生”的背景下，通信网络不仅要更快，还要能针对不同业务提供差异化、确定性保障。意图通信，就是 OPPO 面向 6G 布局的重要技术方向之一。据介绍，作为一种以业务目标而非实现手段为交互对象的端网通信模式，意图通信，旨在让未来网络不仅能够完成数据传输，还能理解用户真正想获得的体验，推动通信从“传数据”进一步走向“传意图”，帮助用户在 6G 时代获得更好的网络体验。据 OPPO 官方描述，未来在演唱会拥塞、游戏卡顿、4K 直播卡顿、云端 AI 应用反应慢等场景中，用户或应用只需描述期望，例如“为这场 4K 直播提供流畅保障”或“为本次游戏对战提供稳定网络服务”，终端即可将需求转化为标准化、可验证的结构化意图，网络再完成意图解析、任务规划和服务调用，用户无需关心底层信令交互与资源调度情况。参考IT之家今日早些时候报道，第九届中国国际进口博览会（进博会）今日正式在上海开幕，高通展示了全球首个 6G 终端原型机。相关阅读：《全球首次展示，高通在进博会公开全球首个 6G 终端原型机》

articles.title: 一汽丰田全新亚洲龙上市，限时权益价 13.38 万元起

articles.title: 美国人形机器人第一股：Agility Robotics 本周登陆纳斯达克，获富士康、英伟达投资
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，据彭博社报道，美国人形机器人企业 Agility Robotics 即将成为美国首家上市的专注于人形机器人的公司，这也标志着这一新兴行业迈出了重要一步。不过，人形机器人行业仍有许多问题有待验证。这家初创公司将于当地时间本周四在纳斯达克挂牌交易，股票代码为“AGLT”。此前，Agility Robotics 已与特殊目的收购公司 Churchill Capital Corp. XI 完成合并。根据公司声明，此次交易完成后，Agility Robotics 手头资金约为 4.65 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 31.09 亿元人民币）（不计相关费用），其中包括由苹果公司主要 iPhone 组装合作伙伴富士康领投的一笔约 2.01 亿美元（现汇率约合 13.44 亿元人民币）私募股权投资。其他知名投资方还包括英伟达、亚马逊和软银愿景基金二期。Agility Robotics 是众多人形机器人研发企业之一。这类机器人以人类为设计原型，通常能够直立行走，也有部分采用轮式移动结构。目前，人形机器人主要应用于仓库和工厂等商业场景。中国企业宇树科技已于今年 8 月在上海上市，而 Agility Robotics 则是首家在美国上市的同类企业。这家总部位于美国俄勒冈州的初创公司目前拥有约 400 名员工，正进一步扩大与 GXO Logistics 的合作，将旗下机器人部署到更多物流设施中。此外，该公司还在与 AGCO 合作开展制造业试点项目。Agility Robotics 首席执行官佩吉 · 约翰逊（Peggy Johnson）在接受采访时表示，随着 AI 从数字世界向现实世界延伸，接下来的发展可能才是更值得关注的部分。她所指的是，人工智能正在被应用于机器人及其他硬件设备。约翰逊表示：“将智能机器人引入更多工作场所，蕴藏着巨大的机遇。当机器与人真正开始协同工作时，许多事情的实现方式都将发生根本性变化。”Agility Robotics 认为，旗下最新款人形机器人 Digit 5 有望缓解劳动力短缺问题，尤其是在仓储行业。这款机器人于今年 9 月发布，能够执行更复杂的工作，例如向设备装载物料、分拣零部件以及检查物品。相比之下，上一代 Digit 4 主要负责堆叠塑料收纳箱等相对简单的任务。Digit 5 还能够在人员附近安全作业，而此前的版本必须在实体安全隔离设施后方运行，这限制了机器人接手人类工作的能力。Agility Robotics 表示，目前已获得超过 3 亿美元（现汇率约合 20.06 亿元人民币）的 Digit 5 多年期订单承诺。该公司的机器人已被 9 家客户投入使用，目前正与 30 多家潜在商业客户进行积极的销售洽谈。这家初创公司已承诺在 12 处客户设施部署 Digit，并计划到 2027 年底，将潜在客户储备扩大至 100 家，覆盖汽车、零售和制药等多个行业。约翰逊援引德勤（Deloitte）2024 年的一项研究指出，到 2033 年，美国制造业无法填补的岗位数量预计将增至约 190 万个。她表示：“Digit 擅长填补的劳动力缺口还在不断扩大。许多企业并不清楚该如何找到足够的人手，来完成那些难以招聘员工、人员流失率又较高的工作。”约翰逊此前曾担任增强现实和混合现实公司 Magic Leap 的首席执行官。她认为，随着华尔街逐步认识这一全新的行业类别，市场仍需要经历一个认知和学习过程。不过，她表示，Agility Robotics 应当按照其他自动化技术供应商的相同标准接受评估，包括作业吞吐量和准确率等指标。她表示：“我认为，一个非常值得关注的地方是，Digit 5 支持通过无线方式升级，我们可以借此教会它新的技能。随着机器人部署到更多场所，我们收集到的数据也会越来越多，这些数据将形成一个不断自我强化的训练循环。”目前，像 Digit 5 这样采用双腿行走的人形机器人仍面临一些独特挑战。与采用轮式移动的类似设备相比，这类机器人运行时的可预测性较低，对周围人员构成的安全风险也更高。约翰逊表示，作为首批上市的人形机器人企业，Agility Robotics 确实感受到了一定压力。她说：“我们是第一个上市的企业，其他公司都会关注我们的表现，不仅会关注相关业绩指标，也会关注安全方面的表现。”不过，她补充称，公司在过去几年于不同环境中开展实际部署的过程中，已经积累了大量经验。约翰逊表示：“演示能够展现技术可以做到什么，但真正的部署才能让你了解哪些方案切实可行。过去三年里，我们学到了很多。如今，我们已经能够进入这些设施，承担实际工作，并通过提供服务获得收入。”

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，DJI 大疆今日正式发布全场景轻型旗舰 DJI Matrice 5T。这是大疆首次在轻型行业无人机上标配激光雷达、毫米波雷达与全彩全向视觉感知系统。中国大陆地区官方售价为 57,488 元。IT之家获悉，该机配备原生 1K 热成像相机、多焦段可见光相机，支持 IP55 防水等级，最长飞行时间达 59 分钟，内置机载算法可辨别超 20 种目标类型，开放算力可以导入第三方 AI 模型，全面覆盖应急救援、电力巡检、测绘、交通、水利海事、公共安全等多类场景。官方表示，这款无人机的运输箱紧凑便携，单手即可轻松提拿；从开机到起飞仅需约 10 秒，可边飞边建模，照片可实时回传遥控器，在本地快速生成点云或 2.5D 模型，200 张照片从采集完成到出图仅需 8 分钟。DJI Matrice 5T 配备高能量密度动力电池，最长飞行时间达 59 分钟。标配静音桨叶采用仿生“蝙蝠翼”前后掠桨尖设计，将飞行噪声控制在 80 dB(A)，在优化飞行能效的同时最大限度降低声学干扰，尤其适用于城市低空巡查和野生动物生态保护观测等对噪声敏感的任务场景。Matrice 5T 是大疆首次在轻型行业无人机上标配激光雷达、毫米波雷达与全彩全向视觉感知系统的机型，三类传感器相互补充。激光雷达在夜间无光环境下仍可捕捉电力导线等细小障碍物，导线探测距离达 32 米。毫米波雷达在团雾、扬尘和雨雪天气中可持续输出距离感知数据，保障复杂天气下的作业安全。在光线和信号受限的环境中，全向低光鱼眼系统在照度低至 0.5 lux 时仍可实现视觉定位。在环境适应与动力方面，该机整机防护等级为 IP55，可在沙尘和雨水喷淋环境下作业，工作温度覆盖零下 20 摄氏度至 50 摄氏度。其动力系统单轴拉力较 Matrice 4T 提升 98%，并搭载电机缺相检测与控制算法，进一步提高稳定性和安全冗余。DJI Matrice 5T 采用新一代图传系统，遥控器内置高增益天线，飞行器内置双 4G 增强图传模块，在 4G 融合图传模式下，可根据网络质量自动选择较优信号链路。遇到山体、建筑遮挡时，可让另一台无人机升空充当“空中信号中转站”：一台中继机可为一台或两台作业机传递信号，两台中继机接力还能进一步延长距离，帮助用户在最远 40 公里的图传距离中把作业范围安全地推向更远、更复杂的地带。DJI Matrice 5T 采用热成像、广角、中长焦、长焦多相机协同配置，并融合激光测距、近红外补光与双光融合显示等辅助能力；其中广角相机在 0.01 lux 微光环境下仍可输出高饱和度全彩影像，长焦相机光学变焦提升至 11 倍。Matrice 5T 无人机智能作业能力较上代大幅提升，内置 AI 模型可辨别超 20 种目标类型，场景适应性更广。可见光与红外画面并行分析、分屏显示，快速检测车、船、烟火点等。更开放机载算力，支持导入第三方机载模型，便于灵活部署专属算法。

articles.title: 比亚迪第二代海豹 07 上市：搭载云辇-M 智能磁流变车身控制系统，超级置换价 13.59 万元起
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，比亚迪第二代海豹 07 正式上市，新车共推出五款车型，官方指导价为 13.99 万-17.29 万元，超级置换价则为 13.59 万-16.89 万元。新车提供纯电与插电式混合动力两种动力形式，搭载天神之眼 B 智能驾驶辅助系统。IT之家注意到，第二代海豹 07 沿用海洋美学 2.0 设计体系，整体风格与海豹 08 保持统一。前脸采用封闭式格栅搭配波浪形分体式大灯，线条简约流畅。车尾则配备与海豹 08 同源的贯穿式尾灯，与前脸造型遥相呼应。新车提供帕拉青、极光粉、海雾紫、琉光银、雪域白、曜石黑共六款车色。车身尺寸上，新车长宽高分别为 5080/1960/1495mm，轴距达 2960mm，座舱空间相比上一代进一步拓展。辅助驾驶方面，天神之眼 C 在纯电尊贵型、旗舰型以及 DM-i 尊贵型上为标配，支持高快领航辅助、拨杆变道、下车泊入、遥控泊车等功能；以上车型也支持天神之眼 B 方案的选装，选装后拥有城市领航辅助（CNOA）功能，当然车顶会增加激光雷达。两款入门的尊享型只有最基础的驾驶辅助系统，比如定速巡航、倒车雷达。内饰方面，新车采用更简洁时尚的全新设计语言，提供云汐白、幻影灰、凝夜紫三款内饰配色。中控区域保留大尺寸悬浮中控屏与液晶仪表，搭配全新三辐式方向盘，中央岛台集成手机无线充电与双杯架。音响系统则配备 20 扬声器的帝瓦雷（Devialet）音响。舒适性配置上，前排搭载具备按摩、通风、加热功能的零重力座椅，后排配备大沙发座椅。储物空间方面，新车提供 618L 后备箱及 160L 前备箱，后者为同级最大。动力方面，DM-i 插混版车型搭载 1.5T 涡轮增压发动机，最大功率 115kW，0-100km/h 加速 7.7 秒，最高车速 190km/h，CLTC 纯电续航最高 330km，满油满电综合续航可达 1700km；纯电版车型全系为后置单电机后驱，最大功率 245kW，0-100km/h 加速 5.5 秒，最高车速 240km/h；电池方面搭载 76.744kWh 第二代刀片电池（支持闪充），CLTC 纯电续航 775km，官方电耗 9.8kWh/100km。底盘方面，新车采用前双叉臂、后五连杆的结构，纯电尊享型与尊贵型、以及两款 DM-i 车型配云辇-C 智能阻尼车身控制系统，纯电旗舰型则采用云辇-M 智能磁流变车身控制系统。

articles.title: 智己 LS8 NEO 纯电版上市：标配全线控灵蜥底盘、宁德时代电池，权益价 23.98 万元起
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，在今晚举行的发布会上，智己 LS8 NEO 纯电版正式上市，共推两款车型，上市权益价 23.98 万元起：93 Max+：上市权益价 23.98 万元103 Max+：上市权益价 25.98 万元IT之家获悉，新车延续了增程版车型的家族化设计语言，全系标配全线控灵蜥底盘以及宁德时代电池。智己 LS8 NEO 纯电版长宽高分别为 5085×2000×1807mm，轴距 3060mm；全系标配全线控灵蜥底盘，搭配四轮转向系统，集成线控转向、线控制动与双向 24° 后轮转向。智能驾驶辅助系统方面，新车搭载 Momenta 物理 AI 世界模型，可选装 520 线超视域激光雷达，拥有 300m 有效感知距离，可选装英伟达 Thor 芯片。内饰方面，智己 LS8 NEO 纯电版整体设计延续增程版车型，采用了与 LS9 同样的家族设计语言。中控台搭载 27.1 英寸 5K 臻彩驾舱屏，副驾前方还搭载了一块 15.6 英寸 3K 副驾娱乐屏。新车第二排配备 21.5 英寸吸顶娱乐屏，采用真 4K 高清分辨率，支持系统级 IMLink 互联控车功能。二排采用柯布西耶电动沙发椅，采用天然乳胶材质，支持靠背角度电动调节，配备折叠小桌板与可伸缩腿托。新车还搭载主驾 4D 机械按摩以及丹麦 B&O 豪华音响。后备厢标准容积可容纳 6 个 28 英寸行李箱，内部宽度可横置高尔夫球包，婴儿车或露营车无需折叠即可放入。全车储物空间共计 9 处，包括二排座椅下方的 9.2L 隐藏式抽屉。动力方面，新车采用纯电驱动，搭载一台最大功率 300 千瓦的电机，电池方面搭载宁德时代 93kWh 和 103kWh 电池组，CLTC 续航里程分别为 684km 和 752km。

articles.title: 全新 smart 精灵#2 正式上市：410 公里续航，限时权益价 9.99 万元起
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，smart 精灵#2 今日正式上市，新车仅提供 Premium 豪华版一个配置版本，限时权益价 9.99 万元起。值得一提的是，该车将同步在欧洲市场推出，其中鎏金高定版车型此前已上市，在中国与欧洲两个市场均限量发售 999 台，官方零售价 112,999 元。IT之家注意到，在外观设计上，smart 精灵#2 向燃油时代的经典车型 smart fortwo（底盘代号 453）致敬，保留了标志性的双门双座布局。车头部分，新车配备集成 LED 日行灯的透镜式大灯，前包围设有大尺寸通风散热开口，中网采用胶囊状孔洞造型，两侧辅以纵向通风口设计。高定版车型则采用哑光云绒白与日冕金双色车漆，并配有专属鎏金印花格栅及车标，以凸显其独特身份。此外，高定版还将搭载 16 英寸鎏金天穹轮圈，并采用前 185/50 R16、后 205/45 R16 的非对称轮胎组合。车身尺寸方面，新车长宽高分别为 2751（2764）/1669/1555mm，轴距为 1875mm，稳居微型车范畴。车尾造型同样颇具看点：不规则圆形尾灯内部采用双条幅光源结构，车顶配有扰流板，并采用分体式天地尾门设计，其中下半部分最大承重可达 120 公斤。进入车内，新车采用 S-Shape 水波纹座舱设计，配备大尺寸悬浮式中控屏，内置 Flyme Link 车机系统，辅以三辐式方向盘、液晶仪表以及怀挡式换挡机构，空调出风口则以涡轮扇叶造型点缀。双座布局下，座椅中央设有隐藏储物格与中央扶手。配置方面，新车提供 256 色氛围灯、方向盘加热、座椅加热、森海塞尔音响系统、L2 级驾驶辅助系统以及遥控泊车等功能。动力与续航方面，smart 精灵#2 搭载一台最大功率 60 千瓦的后置单电机，匹配 35.8kWh 磷酸铁锂电池组，在 CLTC 工况下纯电续航里程可达 410 公里。底盘方面，新车采用前麦弗逊、后五连杆式独立悬架组合，最小转弯半径仅为 3.35 米，在城市狭窄路况下具备出色的灵活性。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，长城汽车董事长魏建军今日宣布，魏牌二代蓝山预售发布会将于 11 月 9 日召开。魏建军表示，在他的理解里，发布会就是要回应用户的所有问题。所以这次魏牌团队想出了更加大胆直接的发布会模式，要做一场最尖锐、最犀利、最直击灵魂的发布会。欢迎大家提问，研发和营销团队会为大家解答。据IT之家此前报道，长城魏牌二代蓝山于 10 月 27 日迎来全球首秀，二代蓝山基于长城归元 S 平台打造。二代蓝山的尺寸根据座位布局有所区分。五座版长宽高为 5140×2050×1960mm，六座版车长增至 5300mm，宽度和高度保持不变，两个版本的轴距均为 3010mm。六座版多出的 160mm 车长主要用于第三排乘坐空间和后备厢容积。动力方面，魏牌放弃了初代的 1.5T 混动，换装 2.0T 发动机，最大功率 182kW，匹配前 110kW、后 220kW 双电机和 4 挡混动专用变速箱。电池容量方面，工信部申报信息显示提供 53.6kWh 和 64.7kWh 两个版本，WLTC 工况纯电续航分别为 220km 和 270km；53.6kWh 版本最高车速为 205km/h，64.7kWh 版本为 210km/h。底盘配备双腔空气悬架和后桥机械差速锁，空气悬架支持车身高度与悬架软硬调节。

articles.title: 科学家在巴西恐龙化石中发现红细胞证据，但未发现 DNA
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，科学家在一块恐龙化石中发现了迄今为止最有力的血细胞存在证据。这块化石来自一只中等体型的肉食性恐龙，其右腿骨骼在约 1.15 亿年前的白垩纪时期形成。当时，这种恐龙曾在今天的巴西境内活动。研究人员在阿拉塔龙（Aratasaurus museunacionali）的骨骼中发现了大量微观结构，这些结构看起来像是已经形成化石的红细胞。此外，他们还检测到了与红细胞关键组成成分有关的化学证据：一种含铁生物分子 —— 血红素。血红素与血红蛋白有关，后者正是赋予血液红色的蛋白质。这些血细胞和血红素的相关证据，来自一只阿拉塔龙骨骼内部的血管通道。研究人员认为，这只恐龙死亡时可能处于幼年或青年阶段，年龄约为 4 岁。作为一种双足行走的恐龙，它的体长约为 3.1 米。该研究负责人、澳大利亚珀斯科廷大学有机地球化学与同位素地球化学家克利蒂 · 格赖斯（Kliti Grice）表示：“我们并没有找到一管恐龙血液。我们看到的是古代生物留下的矿物质和分子层面的回响，而这在科学上更有研究价值。”格赖斯说：“对我而言，最令人惊讶的是，经历了如此漫长的地质年代，我们仍然能够同时观察到这些结构，以及能够证明其生物学来源的化学证据。”据IT之家了解，红细胞由骨髓持续生成，负责将氧气从肺部输送到身体各处的组织，再帮助组织将产生的二氧化碳运回肺部，最终通过呼吸排出体外。与坚硬的骨骼和牙齿不同，肌肉、羽毛等软组织很少能够在化石中保存下来。而血液等体液中的细胞，在化石中更是极为罕见。格赖斯表示：“骨骼和牙齿能够为我们提供大量有关生物解剖结构、生长过程和进化的信息。分子和细胞层面的证据，则有望进一步丰富我们对古代生物的了解。”不过，格赖斯强调，这项研究并未发现恐龙 DNA，并提醒外界不要将此次发现解读为完整恐龙遗传物质得以保存的证据。她表示：“DNA 等大型、包含丰富遗传信息的生物分子，其保存特性与小分子及经过化学转化的分子残留物截然不同。细胞状结构和血红素相关化学信号得以保存，并不意味着细胞中原本存在的 DNA 也留存了下来。”持续探索分子保存的极限研究人员还在阿拉塔龙骨骼中检测到了与胶原蛋白有关的氨基酸。不过，格赖斯指出，这并不意味着科学家已经成功提取出完整的古代蛋白质或遗传信息。胶原蛋白是一种含量丰富的结构蛋白，可以理解为支撑和连接人体组织的“骨架”。格赖斯表示：“这项研究促使我们继续探索分子保存能力的极限，而不是简单地认定，所有生物学信息都会在经过某个时间跨度后彻底消失。”此前，科学家报告发现的最古老 DNA，来自格陵兰岛沉积物中的动物、植物和微生物，其年代约为 200 万年前。据该研究共同作者、巴西国家博物馆古生物学家亚历山大 · 凯尔纳（Alexander Kellner）介绍，这块阿拉塔龙化石是在巴西东北部塞阿拉州的一座石膏矿中出土的，包含部分右侧股骨、胫骨和足部骨骼。格赖斯最后表示：“我们认为，这项研究的独特之处在于多项证据相互印证，且证据链十分有力：恐龙骨骼内部原位保存着大量类似红细胞的结构，这些结构已经矿化，位于骨骼的血管系统中，同时还存在与血红素有关的原位化学证据。据我们所知，此前还没有人在恐龙化石中以这种方式展示过如此完整的一组证据。”这项研究于周一发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》（Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences，PNAS）上。参考资料：https://www.pnas.org/doi/full/10.1073/pnas.2614248123

articles.title: 蔚来李斌：“车电不同寿”问题不能视而不见，要放在 15 年车辆全生命周期去看
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，据华尔街见闻今日报道，蔚来创始人、董事长、CEO 李斌与吉利控股集团董事长李书福在 2026 世界互联网大会乌镇咖荟 · 汽车夜话对话，谈到新能源汽车的 " 车电不同寿 " 问题。IT之家从原报道获悉，李斌表示行业通行的动力电池标准为 8 年 16 万公里健康度保持 70%。他说道：“第 10 年、第 20 万公里后该怎么办？车辆本身还能使用五六年，但电池健康度会大幅下滑，安全风险也随之升高。”此外李斌透露，2012 年至 2014 年他琢磨数年后最终决定做换电，“车电不同寿”放在 5 年、8 年周期里看没那么要紧，拉长到 15 年车辆全生命周期就非常关键。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，上汽集团今日公告，为加强公司高阶智驾技术研发能力，赋能整车产品提升在全球市场的竞争力，董事会审议通过相关决议，拟与延电科技有限责任公司、魔门塔（苏州）科技有限公司（Momenta）共同设立合资公司（名称待定）。IT之家获悉，新公司注册资本 3 亿元，其中：Momenta 认缴出资 1.53 亿元，持股 51%；上汽集团认缴出资 7,500 万元，持股 25%；延电科技认缴出资 7,200 万元，持股 24%。延伸阅读公开工商信息显示，延电科技有限责任公司成立于 2022 年 6 月 27 日，注册资本 1 亿元，法定代表人为臧纯高，其唯一股东为延锋汽车饰件系统有限公司，实际控制人为上海市国有资产监督管理委员会，与上汽集团同属上海汽车工业集团体系。延电科技定位为延锋旗下自主电子业务平台，聚焦智能座舱领域，以座舱域控制器为核心，产品融入交互智能、场景智能与个性化服务，总部位于上海，并在上海、南京设有研发中心，在徐州设有智能制造基地。上汽集团与 Momenta 的合作此前已相当深入。上汽集团是 Momenta 第一大机构股东，Momenta 亦反向持股智己汽车，双方形成“双向持股、战略互嵌”的资本关系；自智己品牌诞生起，其全系车型的辅助驾驶解决方案均由 Momenta 提供，双方联合研发 IM AD 智能辅助驾驶系统。Momenta（魔门塔）成立于 2016 年，2026 年 7 月 8 日在香港交易所主板挂牌上市，股票代码 6880.HK，发行价为 295.6 港元 / 股，上市首日总市值突破 700 亿港元，被称为港股“物理 AI 第一股”，其 CEO 为曹旭东。技术层面，Momenta 将自身定位为物理 AI 基座模型提供商，采用“一个数据飞轮、两条业务腿”的战略，即通过数据驱动算法迭代，同步推进量产自动驾驶与完全无人驾驶业务，2026 年 4 月量产落地 R7 世界模型，支撑乘用车、无人物流车、无人驾驶卡车、无人驾驶出租车及机器人等多场景落地。

articles.title: 嫌不够大气？消息称 Meta 不再使用水果命名 AI 模型
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，据 Business Insider 报道，Meta 不再打算用水果给 AI 模型命名了。一名知情人士透露，这家社交媒体巨头已在内部决定，今后不再以水果为 AI 模型取代号。这一调整主要出于品牌定位方面的考虑。知情人士表示，以水果命名的代号与 Meta 雄心勃勃的 AI 发展目标并不相称。Meta 最新 AI 模型 Wonder Full 的内部代号是“Watermelon”（西瓜）。Meta 称，这是该公司首款达到前沿水平的 AI 模型。此前，Meta 还曾通过发布西瓜照片为这款模型预热。Meta 此前推出的语言模型和图像模型，内部代号分别为“Avocado”（牛油果）和“Mango”（芒果）。上个月，Meta 首席执行官马克 · 扎克伯格（Mark Zuckerberg）和 AI 负责人亚历山大 · 王（Alexandr Wang）在播客节目《Cheeky Pint》中谈到这一命名方式时，还开玩笑称公司已经用完了所有水果名称。扎克伯格表示：“我们已经没有水果名称可用了，所以必须换一种新的命名规则。”王则调侃道：“从体积上来说，唯一比西瓜更大的水果可能就是榴莲了，但你肯定不想用榴莲来命名。”IT之家注意到，Meta 并不是唯一一家使用超市里常见商品为 AI 产品命名的科技公司。据《The Information》2025 年报道，OpenAI 曾在内部将一款 AI 模型命名为“Garlic”（大蒜）。谷歌也在 2025 年推出了名为“Nano Banana”（纳米香蕉）的图像生成工具。近来，随着 AI 模型能力不断增强，科技公司也开始倾向于为其采用更具气势和想象空间的名称，例如 Anthropic 的 Mythos 和 OpenAI 的 Astra。

articles.title: 任天堂 Switch 2 出货量同比下降 41%，但游戏软件销量同比增长 26%
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，任天堂在 2027 财年半年报中透露，公司二季度（即 7 月至 9 月）共出货 267 万台 Switch 2 游戏机，较去年同期的 454 万台下降 41%。初代 Switch 出货量为 61 万台，同比下降 33%。不过任天堂通过软件销量弥补了这部分影响。其中 Switch 2 游戏软件销量同比增长 26%，达到 1503 万份。Switch 2 新作中《斯普拉遁：涂击队》表现突出，销量达到 242 万份；《火焰之纹章：万缕千丝》销量为 134 万份。而初代 Switch 游戏软件销量达到 3192 万份，其中《节奏天国：奇迹之星》贡献了 289 万份销量。数字版游戏销售额同比增长 37%，达到 1,169 亿日元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 49.3 亿元人民币）左右，占软件销售额的 59.8%。

articles.title: 91% ≈ 0%？谷歌最新研究，戳破工程 Agent 的高正确率泡沫
articles.content: 41.3% 的设计项跨过安全门槛，复杂工程仍困于约束耦合。    作者丨郑佳美 岑   峰    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       在工程世界里，91% 的正确，有时和 0% 的交付能力没有区别。一条电缆桥架在机房顶部穿过消防管线，就能让几十页正确的计算书失去交付价值。载流量算对了，电压降符合要求，设备选型也有依据，但进入三维空间后，几套系统争夺同一段净空，工程师只能退回方案。AI Agent 能快速完成局部计算，工程项目却不会按计算题的边界运转：一处调整牵动另一处，刚核验过的结果也可能随修订失效。Google 与 Mercor 近日发布的 Physical-Engineering's Last Exam（PLE），以 85 项机械、电气、土木与结构工程任务量化了这种落差。在 56 项隐藏测试中，Claude Opus 5.5 搭配 Claude Code 得分 48.3%，而在共同创作任务中，它平均满足 91% 的单项约束，只有 41.3% 的交付设计项满足全部硬性安全与可行性要求。更棘手的是，剩下的 9% 往往无法靠继续提高模型的计算能力解决。因为工程设计中的要求彼此关联，解决一个问题，可能又会产生新的问题。PLE 的技术设计恰好揭示了这一困境：当局部能力已经足够强，工程 Agent 究竟还缺少什么？01工程 Agent 正在遭遇可行域瓶颈此前很多 Agent 评测采用逐项累积分数的方式，只要完成更多要求，就能取得更高评价。这适合衡量知识理解和单点执行能力，却会掩盖工程设计中的一类关键失败：模型可能满足了绝大多数要求，但剩下一条恰好决定方案能否投入使用。PLE 在 41 项人机共同创作任务中，将工程约束与设计优化放进同一套评价体系。其中 37 项采用约束评分，在统一评分机制下，40% 的评分空间取决于单项检查通过比例，另外 60% 则与成本或性能优化有关。不过，优化部分存在一个前提：全部硬性安全与可行性约束必须通过。研究团队将其称为硬约束门控（Hard-Constraint Gating）。这个机制有一处关键设计。即使某个方案能够显著降低材料费用，只要违反了一项硬约束，就无法获得成本优化部分的分数。系统仍然记录它已经完成的检查，但不会允许经济收益抵消工程缺陷。PLE 同时设置了合规但未经充分优化的基线方案，以及合规成本的下界。前者用于判断 Agent 是否产生了实际优化收益，后者则为成本改善提供衡量尺度。这样，模型既不能通过选用过量设备轻松满足规范，也无法靠牺牲可行性获得漂亮的成本数字。这种评分方式让一个长期存在的问题变得清晰：工程设计中的优化空间受到约束限制，并且约束之间往往存在联系。例如，在冷却系统设计中，管径决定水力阻力，水力阻力影响水泵工作点，而实际流量又决定换热能力。Agent 如果只根据材料成本缩小管径，后续可能需要更高扬程的水泵，原本节省的费用反而转移到设备和运行能耗上。工程上把所有约束同时成立的设计范围称为可行域。它包含连续变化的参数，也受到设备型号、标准尺寸等离散条件限制。模型每修改一个变量，其他参数能够选择的范围便可能发生变化。这给 Agent 带来一种与普通推理不同的要求。生成候选方案之后，还需要判断当前哪些条件已经接近允许边界，以及下一次修改会影响哪些约束。工程优化中，这些限制进一步调整空间的条件通常被称为活跃约束。PLE 没有直接为 Agent 提供可行域搜索算法，但硬约束门控让这种能力缺口可以被测量。91% 的单项约束满足比例说明，模型已经能够处理大部分局部要求，剩余困难集中在多个条件共同成立，以及满足条件后继续优化。而当设计从单次求解进入长时间、多轮修改时，问题还会继续扩大：此前满足的约束，未必在下一轮操作后仍然有效。02长流程能力正在变成状态一致性问题PLE 的任务环境没有将设计条件整理成一份完整说明。85 项任务累计包含 51

articles.title: Who May Overrule the Agent? Evidence-Gated Authority in LLM Review Institutions
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05390v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent language-model systems often add a reviewer to improve an upstream agent's decision. Yet a reviewer can both repair errors and replace decisions that were already correct. We study this as a problem of institutional jurisdiction: conditional on the same proposal, task information, model, and review output, when is the reviewer authorized to make its recommendation binding? We compare broad override authority with an evidence gate that permits replacement only after the reviewer produces a mechanically valid record of a binding-constraint violation and a compliant repair. Across two locally run open-weight models, 96 spatial-policy tasks, and a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark, the gate sharply reduces corruption of correct proposals while retaining most repairs of violations. articles.title: Agent Harness Awareness: Turning Verified Telemetry into Operational Control for Tool-Using Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05391v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tool descriptions tell an agent what an action can do, but they do not necessarily reveal whether that action is healthy or suitable at the moment of use. Execution harnesses often possess this information through monitors, traces, and recent failures while the model choosing the next action does not. We call this gap operational blindness. We introduce Agent Harness Awareness, a trust-separated design in which the host supplies a small, fresh, verified state snapshot before a consequential action while retaining measurement, enforcement, evaluation, and final dispatch authority. We test its tools-and-network instance with ToolRoute, a controlled isolation benchmark that holds the task and candidate semantics constant and varies the operational information available to the model. In a 216-decision ablation across GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5, and Gemini 3.7 Flash, verified tool-health state reduced mean observable policy regret by 96.9%

articles.title: Uncertainty-Aware Resource Orchestration for Agentic AI Systems
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05392v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems powered by large language models (LLMs) execute as autonomous multi-step pipelines that dynamically invoke tools, integrate observations into memory, and iterate until a task is resolved or a resource budget is exhausted. Unlike classical workflows with fixed graphs, the aggregate compute, bandwidth, and end-to-end latency demands of such pipelines are unknown at dispatch time: they emerge at runtime from intermediate observations and stochastic token sampling, yielding heavy-tailed, multi-modal random variables. This unpredictability forces infrastructure orchestrators into a dilemma: under-provisioning risks mid-execution throttling and deadline violations, while over-provisioning wastes scarce edge or cloud capacity. articles.title: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05393v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models perform strongly on standard medical QA but degrade on harder reasoning tasks, where multi-agent debate often fails to beat strong single-model prompting. We argue that a key limitation is that existing systems select experts and retrieve knowledge from the question alone, rather than from gaps that emerge during reasoning. We propose challenge-aware adaptive recruitment: an external CHALLENGER inspects the evolving reasoning trace and identifies specific factual or expertise gaps. These signals trigger targeted knowledge retrieval or mid-discussion specialist recruitment. On the MEDAGENTSBENCH hard subset (862 questions across nine biomedical datasets), upfront retrieval provides little benefit, while challenge-aware in-between retrieval performs better; on a multi-specialist backbone it improves accuracy on 8 of 9 datasets and adds 6 percentage points over Challenger Only. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05394v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tiered inference distributes large language model computation across a hierarchy of devices, from on-device and edge hardware to the datacenter, and is increasingly offered as the route to cheaper, lower-latency, and more private serving. Most such systems orchestrate frozen model checkpoints, and most decide what to resolve locally and what to escalate using a confidence signal produced by a forward-deployed model. We give a closed-form condition for when no threshold on that signal makes a tiered cascade worthwhile relative to sending every query to the backstop. articles.title: Towards Robust Long-Lived Agents: Benchmarking Experience Lifecycles in Evolving Environments
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05450v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As agents become more capable, they are moving beyond one-off tasks toward sustained assistance across successive user goals. Such assistance requires agents to discover how unfamiliar environments work, reuse what they learn across tasks, and keep that experience current as environments evolve. Existing benchmarks increasingly study experience reuse and adaptation, but provide limited insight into which parts of accumulated experience agents revise, retain, or lose. To address this gap, we introduce ReScopeBench, a benchmark for the experience lifecycle across 18 interactive environments. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05459v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support scientific literature reviews, yet evaluations often examine individual tasks rather than the review process as a whole. We assess six AI tools across four stages: finding relevant articles, interpreting them, synthesizing across them, and proposing future research. The benchmark is a published review of the Spanish plume weather pattern and its 102-article corpus.
  In the initial searches, five tools collectively identified 57 articles, with the best individual tool finding 42. Institutional library access increased discovery from 42 to 82 articles for Codex and from 15 to 79 for Claude Code. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05512v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI Agents are becoming digital coworkers that can browse the web, write code, run experiments, and assist humans over extended horizons. Yet existing benchmarks fall short of real knowledge work: many rely on synthetic data or isolated tasks, missing the complex, multi-party dynamics of collaborative projects, where critical information is scattered across conversations, code, and evolving decisions. Even simple workplace questions may require locating relevant channels and direct messages, recovering context from long discussions, inspecting repository state, reconciling stale or conflicting evidence, and synthesizing across sources.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05524v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose MA-SafeDiffuser, a multi-agent extension of SafeDiffuser that equips diffusion-based trajectory planners with finite-time diffusion invariance guarantees for joint-agent safety specifications. Building on the single-agent construction that embeds control barrier function (CBF) constraints into reverse-diffusion updates, we: (i) formalize joint safe sets as intersections of per-agent and pairwise barrier sets; (ii) derive centralized and decentralized (communication-aware) constrained denoising procedures with provable invariance under mild assumptions; (iii) address local-trap and deadlock phenomena via time-varying specifications and liveness CBFs; and (iv) develop a lightweight benchmarking suite including a multi-agent Maze2D domain. articles.content:

Abstract: We evaluate the extent to which agentic AI models can complete an end-to-end data science project, and how this improves with feedback. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05549v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Transparency has become a central principle in AI governance, yet there is little agreement about what transparency means, for whom, and in what contexts. Drawing on interpretive flexibility within the Social Construction of Technology, this paper examines how different stakeholders understand and experience transparency in generative AI. This study draws from a global survey of 400 end-users, AI builders, and policymakers, complemented by a structured focus group with end-users, grounding the quantitative findings in qualitative insights from the group most underserved by current transparency practice. articles.title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05556v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-as-a-judge is a common substitute for costly human evaluation, and aggregating several judges is the standard remedy for any single judge's bias. Judge pools mix judges of very different reliability, while the human-labeled sets that validate them hold a few hundred items or fewer. In this regime the per-item mean weights weak judges as heavily as strong ones, and confusion-table models such as Dawid-Skene must estimate a per-judge error table from too few items. We propose AGORA (Aggregation Of Reliability-weighted Assessments), an item-response-theory aggregator that places every item on one latent quality scale and describes each judge by a sensitivity parameter and ordered rating thresholds, so judge reliability is learned from all items jointly and without human labels. Across three benchmarks, AGORA matches or exceeds Dawid-Skene on large evaluation sets, and its advantage widens as the set shrinks toward a few hundred items. I

Abstract: Real-world vision is dynamic and scene-rich, while EEG and fMRI resolve it at complementary temporal and spatial scales. Most neural decoding systems, however, align one modality in isolation and mostly against static images or short clips. Abstract: As autonomous AI agents enter permissionless onchain markets, selecting new service providers remains a core challenge. Abstract: Speculative decoding (SD) speeds up large language model (LLM) serving, but its gain depends on the workload's \emph{shape}, such as batch size and context length, and on its \emph{content}. A model-based drafter proposes a short block on any content, while a model-free drafter such as n-gram lookup proposes long copies at almost no cost when the output repeats its input, as in code editing. Adaptive verification spends a batch-wide verification budget on the draft tokens most likely to be accepted, but it supports only one model-based drafter. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05620v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: On Replit, our agentic engineering platform, users now build entire products without writing code, through successive feature requests to an agent. Yet existing coding benchmarks evaluate single, fully specified tasks, and many are near saturation. We introduce ViBench 2.0, a benchmark for long-horizon software building that we use to select our platform's models. Its 17 full-stack web products, modeled on widely used software, grow over 241 feature requests and are judged only when finished, as a user would judge them: a browser agent runs 544 test plans, and a build passes only if every plan does, under a grading protocol validated to keep this strict score reliable. Abstract: Autonomous software agents can act through tools, delegate work, and change their models or execution environments while earlier authorizations remain in flight. We present Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization (ACCA), an approach designed to be harness-independent, for maintaining operational authority according to currently justified assurance. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05436v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spectral graph generation models graphs through the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of their Laplacians, providing a compact and continuous alternative to direct graph construction. However, these eigensystems must retain the structural properties of graph Laplacians. Existing approaches preserve eigenvector orthonormality but do not enforce the Laplacian nullspace constraint, potentially producing eigensystems inconsistent with Laplacian structure. To address this, we introduce Laplacian-Constrained Stiefel Flow Matching (LaSFM), which preserves the nullspace condition alongside eigenvector orthonormality and positive eigenvalues during generation. We characterize the underlying constrained Stiefel manifold and formulate flow matching on it. We further extend LaSFM to property-guided generation, steering samples toward desired graph properties while maintaining these constraints. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05439v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-fidelity simulation of dynamical systems is central to scientific discovery and engineering design, yet remains computationally demanding. Here we introduce the Implicit Neural Operator Solver (INOS), which learns the implicit solve and encodes a time integrator. INOS pretrains a neural operator from static equilibrium solutions and reuses it within Newmark-$\beta$ integration. At each time increment, the integrator forms an effective equilibrium problem, the pretrained neural operator infers the next-step solution field, and the Newmark relations advance the dynamic state. Numerical examples in linear and nonlinear elastodynamics demonstrate accurate full-field predictions without dynamic trajectory supervision. Comparative results show that INOS, evaluated zero-shot, achieves higher predictive accuracy than neural solver baselines trained on dynamic simulations. Abstract: Background: Quantum machine learning (QML) is promoted for clinical prediction, but comparisons with classical models are rarely paired or tested for equivalence. Methods: We compared a quantum-kernel support vector machine (QSVM; 4 qubits, tuned bandwidth) and a variational quantum classifier (VQC) with five tuned classical models across six public clinical datasets. All models used identical four-component inputs and 25 cross-validation splits. Paired AUROC differences were assessed using a corrected resampled t-test, Holm-adjusted equivalence tests (margins: +/-0.02 and +/-0.05), and random-effects pooling. Ablation, noise, finite-shot, and implementation-fault analyses were conducted. We propose QML-Health-READY, an eight-domain reporting framework. articles.title: Objective-Conditioned Active Preference Learning for Multi-Objective Alignment
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05506v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with several objectives, such as helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty, typically relies on preference judgment for each objective, growing the annotation cost linearly with the number of objectives. Active preference learning can reduce this cost by selecting the comparisons whose labels are expected to change the policy most. Existing remedies either lack an objective-aware query selection mechanism for the multi-objective setting or regard conflicting preferences as harmful, therefore excluding them from the training data. We introduce OGC-DPO (Objective-conditioned Gradient Coverage DPO), an active learning framework that treats each (response pair, objective) combination as a separate query and measures its informativeness through the policy's own implicit gradient, without relying on an external reward model. OGC-DPO then selects the queries that most expand each objective's gradient coverage.

Abstract: Textual information is ubiquitous in real-world time series datasets, appearing as news, reports, and annotations that hold key predictive signals not deducible from numerical history alone. Abstract: Across a wide range of applications, kernel measures are used to tune hyperparameters, select among candidate kernels, and assess the suitability of kernels for specific learning tasks. Many existing kernel measures, such as alignment to the ideal kernel, are designed to reward kernels which captures all samples from the same class as similar. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05546v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) eliminates the central aggregation server but remains vulnerable to data heterogeneity, Byzantine attacks, and channel noise. We show that noise accumulates as models propagate across nodes, becoming increasingly significant as the learning rate decays. Moreover, accumulated noise enables Byzantine attackers to exploit loss-based model selection by mimicking honest model averages. To address these challenges, we propose screened, hop-aware, ranked, proximal averaging, a robust DFL framework (FedSharp). In this approach, each node maintains models from its 2b predecessors, ensuring at least b honest candidates when at most b nodes are Byzantine. articles.content:

Abstract: Support vector machines (SVMs) are fundamentally grounded in geometric margin maximisation and currently lack a mainstream probabilistic interpretation. In this paper, we bridge this gap by proving that the dual objectives of both support vector classification and support vector regression are exact, constrained Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence minimisation tasks between two Gaussian measures. We further show that this same divergence formulation recovers the exact objective function for kernel ridge regression when domain constraints are removed and $L^2$ regularisation is applied. Abstract: Data tends to be most useful when it is shared, and the data most worth sharing is often the data that privacy obligations restrict. Abstract: A deep RL agent trained on a fixed persona reward plays one way: an Explorer keeps exploring while starving, a Survivor hoards on an empty map. Since each persona fixes its own reward, automated playtesting trains N agents for N styles. articles.title: Transport along Local Annealing Paths: Wasserstein Geometry and Multimodal Sampling
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05605v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Variational approaches to learning transport maps for multimodal sampling can suffer from mode collapse. One way to mitigate this problem is to learn transport along a prescribed path of intermediate distributions defined by geometric annealing. We show that annealing can take a substantial detour in Wasserstein space: when mass moves between modes, the path can be much longer than the distance between its endpoints. We further link path geometry to transport learning, showing that long annealing paths can slow population optimization, while sufficiently regular paths permit rapid convergence. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05616v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training on large datasets motivates selecting which examples receive expensive training computation. Fixed quotas determine the amount of pruning in advance, while absolute confidence cutoffs depend on the score scale. We study a population-relative alternative that adapts the threshold and retained count together. We introduce LACS (Label-Agnostic Confidence Selector), a training-time rule based on maximum predictive confidence, requiring neither labels at selection time nor per-example gradients. LACS removes examples at or above a log-mean-exp reference plus a margin. We characterize its sensitivity to score gaps and mass, and derive an exact no-pruning condition. For $0<\rho<1$, the removed fraction is at most $\rho$ and at least one example remains. The unsigned score permits both confidently correct and confidently wrong examples to be removed. Abstract: Large-scale ranking and recommendation models of Web platforms benefit from increased compute much as large language models do, and their scaling behavior is broadly power-law in form. Abstract: A central challenge in assistive brain-to-robot control is decoding a user's latent intent from complex and noisy brain signals. Prior approaches evaluate decoders as single-trial classifiers with accuracy-based metrics, but this neglects the inherently sequential nature of assistive control. Abstract: Legislative hearings are distinct communication events with their own human recognizable structure and logic, yet they have been analyzed as distinct phenomena beyond their transcripts. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05382v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Misinformation spreads faster than professional fact-checkers can manually verify it and write articles explaining their verdicts. This creates a need to automate the production of fact-checking articles. This paper details work done by the DS@GT ARC team for CLEF 2026 CheckThat! Lab Task 3 Fact-Checking Article Generation. We seek to generate a full fact-checking article from a claim, its original verdict, and a set of scraped source documents. Our team built a four-stage pipeline that cleans noisy evidence, retrieves and clusters relevant sources, generates the article by conditioning \texttt{Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct} on the original fact-checker verdict, and recovers inline citations through deterministic post-processing. We achieved a mean score of 0.428 and ranked 3rd out of 9 teams for the CLEF 2026 CheckThat! Lab Task 3, compared to a baseline mean score of 0.272. Abstract: Generalisability is a central question for deep neural networks, including the cross-language generalisation of speaker embeddings. Embeddings exhibited cross-language generalisation that broadly paralleled human behaviour, reflecting accurate identity discrimination and sensitivity to language switching. Abstract: Automated detection of machine-generated text is applied where the verdict carries a cost for the author, yet origin is a property of the production process, not an observable property of the text. The Russian-language corpus of 1882 documents comprises a machine part, generated by four generation channels (each backed by its own model family) across 45 tasks in three task modes, and an archival human part annotated for source regimentation level before the texts were read. Abstract: Small Language Models (SLMs) are increasingly deployed on consumer-grade hardware, yet their ability to preserve information across progressively longer contexts remains insufficiently understood. Abstract: For humans, referential disambiguation is a collaborative process involving clarification questions asked when they will meaningfully change the outcome. However, large language models (LLMs) have been shown to be biased toward premature answering, preferring definite single-turn responses over more clarification exchanges. In this paper, we study the problem of "strategic clarification" -- asking clarification questions in a reference game when their answers will narrow the set of candidate referents. We construct a controlled test environment from the SIMMC 2.1 dataset that records how many questions each ambiguous reference needs to be successfully resolved, and examine how baseline LLM behavior and common post-training methods ask clarifying questions vs. attempt to answer the referent. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05539v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLMs can repair noisy OCR transcripts of historical documents, but they also change text that was already correct. We propose EditVeto, a veto gate placed after a full-context LLM rewrite. The rewrite is character-aligned to the OCR input, its differences are split into blocks, and a 0.6B-parameter gate keeps or reverts each block. An oracle analysis motivates the design: given the true error locations, per-span generation is worse than no correction, whereas vetoing a full rewrite's edits helps. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05596v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Different retrievers exist for retrieval-augmented generation, yet none performs best for all queries. Therefore, the key question is: given a query and retrieved passages from different retrievers, which one is most suited for that query? Existing routers usually make predictions from query-specific features and a fixed pool of retrievers; such routers have no output for an unseen retriever and are incapable by design on a new corpus. To fill these gaps, RAGCompass reads the retrieved passage sets themselves: passages from an unfamiliar retriever or corpus stay directly comparable to other passages, so routing stays well designed where a query-only map would fail. We contrastively fine-tune a reranker against the answer each evidence set produces, which accounts for most of the gain; a small comparison head adds a moderate improvement, and neither component has retriever-specific parameters. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05731v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most memory systems for LLM agents are retrospective, preserving and retrieving past information to inform current decisions. Proactive agents, however, also require prospective memory: retaining future-directed intentions and realizing them when appropriate opportunities arise, even without explicit requests. Crucially, remembering the right intention does not guarantee acting at the right time: a related observation may call for waiting, while a later cue may make the same intention actionable. Inspired by cognitive theories of human prospective memory, we introduce Pro-Memory, a memory framework that separates maintaining future intentions from deciding when and how to realize them. Pro-Memory preserves pending objectives linked to their supporting evidence, assesses new observations against their original goals and activation conditions, and coordinates appropriate contributions with the agent's ongoing actions. arXiv:2611.05380v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Visual autoregressive generation spans two dominant paradigms: next-scale prediction for images and video, and next-frame prediction for video. Both decode block-by-block rather than token-by-token, yielding KV caches whose statistics diverge from those of language models. At scale, KV memory exceeds the weights and limits large-scale deployment caused by a large amount of visual tokens. Our analysis of these caches reveals three findings. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05404v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The hand localization problem has been a longstanding focus due to its many applications. The task involves modeling the hand as a singular point and determining its position within a defined coordinate system. However, due to data modality limitations, existing hand localization technologies face several challenges. For example, vision-based localization raises privacy concerns, while wearable-based methods compromise user comfort. In this paper, we introduce mmHand, a new device-free, privacy-preserving dynamic hand localization system with pixel-level accuracy, using a single commodity mmWave device. We first propose a mmImage generation tool to fully extract spatial information from raw mmWave data and introduce a novel 2D image-format representation of mmWave data. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05406v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Contrastive pretraining has advanced image-text understanding, yet image, video, and audio encoders are still trained independently, with cross-modal alignment realized mainly through post-hoc binding to a frozen anchor space. We present Omni-Encoder, a general multimodal encoder that processes image, video, audio, and audio-visual inputs within a single SigLIP-2 Vision Transformer with fully shared parameters. Unlike anchor-centric binding or per-modality adapters, all modalities are optimized jointly end-to-end, and the framework is organized from input to training. A modality-native input stage first maps each signal into the shared embedding space, including a 1D-convolutional audio tokenizer that converts mel-spectrograms into tokens aligned with visual patches. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05407v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion image generators are successful due to accurate denoising networks and strong numerical samplers. Yet the two components are not fully matched. During sampling, the denoiser predicts for the next step based on flawed input that differ much from the real data. This train-test gap, or exposure bias, caps image generation quality (i.e., blurry, lacking in details or awkward in shape). To mitigate the problem, we propose PEEK, a novel training-free deterministic sampler plugin. At each eligible denoising step, PEEK first performs a provisional one-step update, evaluates the denoiser once at the look-ahead state, and interpolates it with the one-step-later prediction to form the next noisy state. By taking the additional step, we obtain a generally more-image-like prediction from the higher-signal noisy state, mitigating the exposure bias. Abstract: Low-textured sketch images are widely used in scientific applications, including wildlife conservation, archaeological illustration, and forensic composites. Learning from and retrieving such images is challenging because they lack detailed surface textures and visual variations commonly exploited by modern deep learning models. This paper proposes Augmentation with Reinforcement Transformation (ART) to fine-tune pretrained models to learn effective representations for accurate sketch image retrieval. Our key observation is that sketches are particularly sensitive to image transformations, such as rotation, flipping, zooming, and stretching. Abstract: Point cloud denoising aims to recover clean geometry from noisy 3D observations while preserving both fine surface details and the underlying spatial distribution of the points. Many learning-based methods adopt a two-stage pipeline that first extracts point-wise features from the noisy input and subsequently predicts point-wise displacements via simple regressions. However, these approaches often lack robust feature guidance and distribution-aware geometric refinement, causing them to fail at maintaining optimal point uniformity and geometric quality. To address these limitations, we propose PointNDF, a denoising framework that combines patch-level geometric context with local displacement prediction. Abstract: Surgical world models have the potential to provide intra-operative guidance, accelerate risk-free training and facilitate transfer of expert surgical maneuvers. However, the use of world models for transferring surgical expertise has been largely unexplored. Moreover, recent approaches in this domain have mainly relied on ground truth kinematics actions or expert annotations for specific tasks, limiting their applicability beyond the narrow range of tasks with ground-truth annotations. In contrast, existing works in the natural domain have shown promising results in learning latent actions solely from unlabeled videos and transferring the learned actions across contexts. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05449v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Learning on boundary representations (B-reps) requires robustness to the pose of a part, since CAD models are not stored in a canonical orientation. Existing B-rep networks either operate on world-frame coordinates and normals, and thus degrade under rotation, or encode each face in a local reference frame. Local frames yield invariance, but reduce inter-face messages to scalars and discard the relative orientation of adjacent faces. We propose SO3brep, an SO(3)-equivariant graph neural network on the B-rep face-adjacency graph. Node features are computed in local frames and mapped into a shared frame by Wigner D-matrices. Clebsch-Gordan tensor products couple these features with the directions between adjacent faces, so that relative orientation is preserved throughout message passing and the output remains SE(3)-invariant. articles.title: From Tokens to Trajectories: Parameter-Efficient Continuous Adaptation of Unified Multimodal Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05451v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While discrete tokenization in Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) establishes strong semantic reasoning, it introduces a strict quantization bottleneck that degrades fine-grained visual details, often resulting in structurally accurate but artifact-heavy images. We introduce FlowShift, a parameter-efficient post-training framework that bypasses this bottleneck by converting pre-trained discrete UMMs into continuous rectified-flow generators. Instead of discarding the backbone's semantic priors, FlowShift replaces discrete visual interfaces with continuous latent projections and applies LoRA to the attention layers. To efficiently boost visual quality without semantic drift, we propose Dual-Objective Velocity Vector Distillation (DOVD), which aligns the model with a high-fidelity continuous teacher and ground-truth continuous trajectories. This approach drastically improves perceptual quality while preserving prompt adherence and reasoning.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05522v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose visual representations into individual features, offering a promising basis for explaining model behavior. Interpreting these features typically relies on images or pixel regions that most strongly activate them. However, this evidence becomes ambiguous when multiple features with different semantics frequently activate in the same locations, such as texture and color in the same patterns. We propose Reconstructive SAE Intervention (RecSAEI), a framework that shifts feature explanation from passive observation to active visual reconstruction. By intervening on representations along SAE decoder directions and reconstructing the visual output, we provide direct evidence of a feature's semantic meaning. We demonstrate that our method successfully disambiguates feature meanings across multiple datasets and vision encoders. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05559v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In biodiversity monitoring, a single image raises several questions: which taxon, how many, which trait, and whether the individual has been seen before. Vision-language models (VLMs) could answer all of these from the image, but their ability is largely untested in biology, as existing benchmarks focus mostly on species identification within a few taxonomic groups. We present Bio-VQA, the largest biological visual question answering (VQA) benchmark and the only one to span four aspects of biological visual understanding: hierarchical taxonomic reasoning, fine-grained attribute grounding, quantitative spatial reasoning, and individual re-identification. Bio-VQA contains 1.86M questions over 217K images from 11 public datasets, and extends right-or-wrong scoring to graded scoring, so a near-miss counts for more than a distant one. Automated MTV is useful only if its estimate is reliable for the individual patient, yet segmentation models are usually evaluated with overlap metrics such as Dice rather than burden error. Abstract: Contrastive vision-language models score left/right relations near chance, but the symptom has two causes that call for opposite repairs: the relation may survive in the pooled embedding yet be unreachable by native image-text similarity, or pooling may discard it while the dense features retain it. On clean two object photographs, across ten encoders, the lateral polarity is linearly decodable from the flip odd component of the pooled vector at 0.77-0.99, yet a search over a million captions leaves nine of the ten at chance under native scoring: an access failure. Abstract: Point cloud segmentation is a fundamental task in 3D data analysis, with applications across robotics, augmented and virtual reality, and remote sensing. However, the inherent sparsity, noise, and unordered nature of point clouds introduce significant challenges, particularly in achieving reliable classification. While the state-of-the-art rely on training models for explicit modeling of uncertainty, there is a gap in exploring different roles that estimated uncertainty using generative approaches can play. This work investigates the impact of deterministic uncertainty in point cloud segmentation by explicitly modeling epistemic uncertainty and using it in different roles, namely, as a feature and in loss function. Abstract: Remote sensing change detection is typically formulated as Siamese feature comparison, where two images are encoded independently and a decoder determines which discrepancies correspond to meaningful change. This is challenging because the encoders preserve both true scene changes and nuisance variations such as illumination, seasonal, radiometric, and geometric differences. We introduce ChangeJEPA, a bitemporal joint-embedding predictive architecture that reformulates change detection as latent post-state prediction. Given a pre-change image and partial post-change evidence, ChangeJEPA predicts the full post-change representation under two complementary conditions: a prior hypothesis derived from the pre-change scene and an updated hypothesis conditioned on observed post-change context. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05578v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) systems serve users across languages and cultural contexts. However, evaluations of cultural representation focus mainly on recognizable elements such as landmarks, clothing, and activities, overlooking the cultural values that generated images convey. To bridge this gap, we introduce VisionValueBench, a multilingual benchmark that operationalizes six of Hofstede's cultural value dimensions (e.g., individualism versus collectivism) to investigate how T2I systems frame neutral social situations through a particular cultural orientation. We find that value-neutral prompts, which admit diverse cultural interpretations, nonetheless yield images that favor particular value orientations, a phenomenon we call visual value leakage. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05593v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Can a neural network learn to render 3D Gaussian splats on its own, with no rasterizer in the renderer? We present GaussianRenderFormer, a transformer that takes a set of Gaussians and a camera and outputs the image directly. Each Gaussian becomes one token in a view-independent encoder, and a view-dependent decoder turns small patches of camera rays into pixels by attending to those tokens. Trained on 26,820 Objaverse objects pruned to 20,000 Gaussians each, GaussianRenderFormer renders 300 unseen objects at 38.08 dB PSNR against the full, unpruned splats, while rasterizing the same pruned input reaches 44.02 dB. The gap is not one of generalization, and our diagnostics are consistent with a bottleneck in the view decoder: telling it the projected footprint of each Gaussian, which it could in principle infer, adds 1.4 dB. Under-training is not ruled out. Code, trained models and videos: https://svlwoof.github.io/gaussianrenderformer

articles.content:

Abstract: Grounding a text query in an image needs a matrix scoring every term against every patch. Vision-language models compute it with an aligned text encoder, which many image encoders, such as histopathology-related models trained on slides alone, lack. The Caption-Anchored Patch-Term Occurrence Representation (CAPTOR) estimates the matrix without a text encoder. It clusters a frozen image encoder's patch tokens into visual words and describes each captioned image by its share of patches in each word. A term signature is the standardized difference of those shares between images whose captions mention the term and the rest. The matrix factorizes into a term-by-word table and a query-independent image factor, so an image is encoded once and a new term adds one table row. Abstract: Despite growing interest in foundation models for robotic manipulation, systematic evaluation of their capabilities remains elusive. Existing benchmarks are either narrow and saturated, offering little signal on SOTA methods, broadly scoped, providing diversity at the cost of controlled experimentation, or require training on large, messy open-source datasets. We introduce MESA, an evaluation framework designed for precise, reproducible measurement of language-conditioned policy generalization. Abstract: Robot imitation learning is limited by the scarcity of action-labeled data, while action-free demonstrations such as videos are abundant. Recent latent-action methods learn action-relevant representations from observation transitions, but they do not optimize latent actions for downstream control, leading to latent representations that are difficult for policies to model and difficult to accurately decode into continuous robot actions. This paper introduces ELA, an end-to-end framework for learning from video demonstrations via latent actions jointly optimized for policy learning and action decoding. ELA jointly trains a latent action model, latent action policy, and action decoder, enabling policies to leverage abundant video data with only a handful of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Abstract: This letter presents a trajectory planner for humanoid robots to perform dynamic motions on complex, parameterizable terrains using a contact-implicit whole-body optimization framework. The planner generates feasible movements without predefined contact sequences, considering the robot's full dynamics and kinematics. To plan bipedal locomotion on steps, ramps, and other terrains, we propose a mathematical model to approximate ground geometry with a smooth surface. The rigid interaction between the robot and the ground is modeled via novel contact constraints, extending the domain of applicability from flat and horizontal surfaces to any arbitrary smooth surface. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05615v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High motion performance and avoiding structural vibrations rely on smooth trajectory planning. The smoothness requirement depends on the robot's complexity in terms of the number of degrees of freedom and system order due to the flexibility of the joints and links. For industrial robots, the smoothness requirements have been determined and subsequently taken into account. Abstract: Olfaction provides critical information about airborne chemical cues, yet it remains largely underexplored in embodied AI, with limited prior machine olfaction work focusing primarily on semantic odor perception. Abstract: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05793v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Short-horizon model predictive control (MPC) is fast but myopic. ZipMPC compensates by learning a context-dependent correction of the short-horizon cost that imitates a long-horizon expert. Abstract: Assessing the deployment performance of learned robot policies during training is challenging, as directly measuring task success requires costly real-world trials for each candidate checkpoint. Abstract: The optimal rapidly exploring random tree (RRT*) is proven asymptotically optimal on open subsets of Euclidean space with straight-line local planning. Abstract: An ordered sequence of end-effector poses can give a redundant robot arm multiple valid joint configurations at each waypoint. Inverse kinematics (IK) computes these configurations. A learned model removes paths whose transitions are likely to cause self-collision. Abstract: Off-policy deep reinforcement learning trains on random samples from a replay buffer of past experience. articles.content:

Abstract: Integrating six-axis tactile feedback into robotic interfaces requires compact sensors with accurate load measurement and rapid online reconstruction. This paper presents LumiTac, a low-profile, camera-free optoelectronic tactile sensor combining spatially distributed illumination with spectral encoding. A compact multilayer perceptron reconstructs three force and three moment components from 20 optical channels. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05938v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Visual-inertial odometry relies on visual features that correspond to 3D points with consistent projections across sequential frames. articles.title: Learning Object-Centric Motion Priors from Human for Robotic Dexterous Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05979v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Manipulating diverse objects with multi-fingered dexterous hands is challenging due to the high dimensionality and complex dynamics. Human-Object Interaction (HOI) datasets provide rich knowledge about task information and embodied interactions. Instead of solely imitating the human demonstrations, our method learns to holistically predict future hand-object states by leveraging these datasets. The predicted future states of the object can serve as a general-purpose reward term for reinforcement learning, reducing reliance on task-specific reward engineering and enhancing generalization across tasks. We conduct extensive experiments on three manipulation tasks in simulation and the real world. Our approach outperforms existing SOTA methods in both success rate and generalizability on novel objects. Furthermore, we validate the cross-embodiment compatibility of our methods by successfully deploying the skills on different robot hands.

articles.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
articles.content: Vision-language-action models are typically built on a simple premise: perception is first compressed by visual encoders, and action reasoning begins only afterwards. Yet manipulation often hinges on precisely the visual signals most vulnerable to this abstraction, e.g., local geometry, boundaries, depth, and subtle state changes. This raises a fundamental question: should action policies inherit a fixed visual endpoint, or directly access evolving visual computation? We introduce NEO-VLA, a structurally encoder-free vision-language-action framework. Images are tokenized by lightweight patch convolutional layers and evolve jointly with language throughout the backbone, allowing a flow-matching action expert to draw from instruction-conditioned visual representations at different depths. This simple change reveals a consistent pattern. Native architectures outperform encoder-based counterparts under controlled comparisons; full fine-tuning reduces but does not erase the gap, and additional scale alone cannot recover it. More strikingly, layer-wise probing shows that the action-critical signals often peak well before the final visual representation. Across diverse manipulation settings and distribution shifts, NEO-VLA consequently achieves stronger and more robust control. Together, these results suggest that embodied control benefits from access to visual representations across the computational hierarchy, rather than a fixed encoder output.

articles.title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents
articles.content: Researchers use large language models as agents in social simulations, where agents are prompted with observations and background information intended to shape their actions. Yet LLM agents have been shown to substantially change their behavior under meaning-preserving prompt variations, creating a validation problem for social simulation. One plausible hypothesis is that this brittleness reflects a lack of grounding and can be reduced by enriching the context provided to the agents. Whether richer context improves robustness remains unclear, in part because context richness and robustness are rarely defined in ways that support controlled comparisons. We address the first need with controlled context enrichment, a set of prompt substitution rules that systematically enriches distinct types of context: neutral padding, generic social background, descriptive decision grounding, and normative decision grounding. We address the second by introducing selective robustness as a validation criterion: insensitivity to meaning-preserving prompt variation combined with a directional response to decision-relevant changes in the social world. We demonstrate the framework in a Prisoner's Dilemma-like game, showing how it can be used to identify which forms of context enrichment produce more desirable and robust agent behavior. We find that these forms of enrichment produce distinct behavioral patterns that vary between the two models tested.

articles.title: cuRoboV2-Fast: Fast Torque-Limited Collision-Free Motion Planning
articles.content: We present cuRoboV2-Fast, a GPU-accelerated planner that reduces both planning latency and execution time for collision-free, payload-aware, torque-limited motions. B-spline trajectory optimization reduces the required iterations, while accelerated robot computations and differentiable inverse dynamics reduce refinement cost and accommodate changing payloads. TimeOpt optimizes traversal speed along the fixed path under sampled velocity, acceleration, jerk, and torque constraints, exploiting local spline support to solve banded Newton systems efficiently on the GPU. With a 3,kg payload, cuRoboV2-Fast achieves 4.4 ms mean planning time on RTX 5090, 14.7x faster than cuRoboV2. Our method on Jetson AGX Orin plans faster than cuRoboV1 + TOPPRA on RTX 5090. A stereo-camera-based deployment on YAM achieves 5.93 s mean completed pick-and-drop cycles, 34.6% shorter than cuRoboV2. Code (Apache 2.0): www.github.com/NVlabs/curobo , Project Page: www.research.nvidia.com/labs/lpr/curobov2-fast .

articles.title: FlowReconBench: Accuracy, calibration and cost of learned and classical flow reconstruction from sparse sensors
articles.content: Reconstructing full flow fields from sparse sensors requires prior assumptions about unmeasured regions and physical variables. Yet it remains unclear when learned models outperform classical estimators and which aspects of their predictions can be trusted. FlowReconBench evaluates ten learned and five classical methods on three regimes: a laminar cylinder wake across Reynolds numbers, two-dimensional Kolmogorov turbulence and a large-scale three-dimensional (3D) isotropic turbulence. Methods share leakage-controlled splits and sensor draws and are scored on per-channel error, ensemble spread, calibration, spectra and cost. The leading method changes for each regime. Classical methods perform strongly in low-order and dense-sensing regimes. On the cylinder wake, linear stochastic estimation and gappy proper orthogonal decomposition lead, including for unobserved pressure. In 3D, inverse-distance weighting matches the best learned methods on observed channels. Data-driven methods become superior at decreasing sensor density or poor sensor observability. On Kolmogorov flow, continuous ranked probability score and error yield different method rankings: generative models offer broader but underdispersed ensembles, while deterministic models prioritize pointwise error. Generative models balance this tradeoff through their sampler budget, with a larger budget improving ensemble quality at higher computational cost. In 3D, scaling tests demonstrate that queryable methods are flat in memory, while full-grid construction methods run out of memory. Observing only 2 of 4 fields leaves the problem kinematically underconstrained, yet a latent model can reproduce structural similarities to the ground truth.

articles.title: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories
articles.content: Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories (SDCLs) are moving chemical experimentation toward embodied automation, where machines must perceive laboratory scenes, reason about experimental states, and act under physical, procedural, and safety constraints. Although Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly considered as embodied brains for such systems, existing laboratory benchmarks mainly focus on safety, anomaly detection, or general scientific understanding, leaving their execution-oriented embodied capabilities underexplored. To fill this gap, we introduce BEAKER, a Benchmark for evaluating Embodied Actionability, Knowledge, Experimentation, and Reasoning in SDCLs. BEAKER contains 1,000 expert-curated question-answer samples across 11 image and video task types, covering key judgments required for chemical laboratory execution, including affordance grounding, trajectory planning, equipment, state, and safety recognition, apparatus setup, operation and step reasoning, and temporal procedure reasoning. All questions and annotations are manually created and reviewed by chemistry and embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) experts, without AI-assisted generation or annotation. We evaluate 28 general-purpose, science-oriented, chemistry-specialized, and embodied MLLMs in an offline, single-turn setting. Results show that current models can follow coarse experimental procedures in videos, but still struggle to ground actions into operable regions and feasible trajectories, to recognize fine-grained laboratory apparatus, states, and safety norms, and to order steps in mid-length procedures. BEAKER thus reveals a clear gap between coarse procedural understanding and the precise, action-grounded perception required for laboratory execution, providing a diagnostic benchmark for future MLLMs in SDCLs.

articles.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
articles.content: AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research. However, existing physics benchmarks only evaluate fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely check research quality alongside correctness. We introduce FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. Each task requires agents to review the literature, develop a research plan, conduct research and experiments, and produce structured outputs and scientific manuscripts. Combining deterministic verifiers with expert-authored rubrics, FrontierPhysics evaluates whether agents' research is correct and publishable. Across 22 models in 26 configurations, no configuration passes more than 46 of its 168 rollouts. Manual review of agent trajectories shows that frontier agents' main weaknesses are insufficiently rigorous reasoning and limited expert intuition, rather than gaps in physics knowledge or execution errors.

articles.title: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
articles.content: Humanoid robots have the potential to automate a wide range of physical tasks. Progress toward generalist humanoid autonomy, however, remains constrained by a data bottleneck: mapping pixels and free-form language to low-level joint commands requires paired supervision, and no corpus of such data exists at sufficiently large scale. Some approaches rely on human teleoperation and wearable capture devices, which require at least an hour of human time to produce an hour of data. We present HALO, a humanoid autonomy system powered by a pipeline that synthesizes vision-language-motion data across a thousand procedurally generated homes. The corpus scales with compute rather than human labor. HALO acquires a repertoire of physical skills, including sitting on chairs, navigating to named objects, stepping sideways through half-open doors, crouching and crawling beneath tables, and pushing boxes. It orchestrates these skills to solve composite, long-horizon tasks. Without ever seeing a real home during training, HALO transfers zero-shot to the physical world, achieving a 91% success rate across 360 trials in six unmapped real-world environments. See https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-halo/ for code and videos.

articles.title: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement
articles.content: The introduction of generalist robot policies has enabled a single, large model to learn to perform a variety of tasks from a vast pre-training corpus. While these models often exhibit powerful zero-shot generalization capabilities, they typically require an adaptation phase to achieve sufficient performance in deployment. Iterated self-improvement via reinforcement learning (RL) has demonstrated promise in enabling this adaptation, yet such approaches have been largely explored in single-task settings - where the goal is to simply improve on a narrow deployment task - which lies in stark contrast to the multi-task capabilities of the base policy. In this work we ask whether generalist robot policies are capable of multi-task, generalist improvement in deployment - targeting many diverse tasks simultaneously - and what algorithmic recipe enables this. To answer this question, we first develop a set of structured evaluations to test generalist improvement capabilities, and systematically evaluate algorithmic and practical design choices regarding value estimation, policy extraction and resource allocation. We show that not only can generalist policies be improved online across diverse tasks, but that the right recipe can enable generalization and increase performance on tasks not considered during online training. We characterize when this generalization occurs and show that both the training task distribution and the use of value-based RL are critical. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first evidence for online generalist improvement for robot foundation models.

articles.title: Motion-guided Contrastive Regularization For Latent World Models
articles.content: JEPA-style world models learn action-conditioned latent dynamics without reconstructing observations, but distributional regularization alone does not ensure that their representations preserve information needed for control. We identify static collapse, a failure mode in which the encoder preserves episode-specific static content while suppressing manipulation-relevant state changes. Because static content is temporally predictable yet diverse across episodes, this failure can persist despite regularizers such as SIGReg. A controlled study on OGBench-Cube shows that introducing randomized backgrounds substantially degrades planning performance while leaving the underlying manipulation task unchanged. To address this problem, we propose motion-guided contrastive regularization. Our approach compares predicted latent transitions with transitions to candidate observations from the same episode, reducing the usefulness of static background identity for distinguishing action outcomes. Optical-flow similarities provide soft contrastive targets, allowing candidates with similar motion to receive similar supervision. Combined with latent prediction and SIGReg, our objective encourages representations to preserve within-episode state distinctions and similarities between related transitions. Our method improves planning success over LeWorldModel (LeWM) from 52% to 78% on OGBench-Cube with randomized backgrounds and from 14% to 54% on LIBERO-Object, while maintaining comparable performance on four other visual-control benchmarks.

articles.title: Occlusion for Free: Detecting Occlusion from the Disagreement Between Two Monocular Distance Cues
articles.content: Knowing that a pedestrian is occluded is useful to a robot even when the detector cannot recover the hidden pixels, but occlusion estimators are normally trained on occlusion annotations that deployment settings rarely have. We show that occlusion can be read off two distance estimates a camera-only pipeline already computes. Apparent height is largely unchanged by occlusion, because the detected box still spans the whole person; monocular metric depth is pulled toward the occluder, because the nearest surface inside the box is what a depth map reports. Only their ordering matters, so no focal length, stature, or depth scale is needed, provided the depth model's error is close to a pure gain, a condition that can be checked without labels. The score detects heavy occlusion on KITTI with AUC 0.909 (0.888 over all annotated pedestrians, including those the detector misses), requires no training and no occlusion labels, and is not a proxy for range: within fixed distance bands it holds AUC 0.894-0.925 while true distance alone sits near chance. On synthetic CARLA scenes with measured visibility it reaches 0.819, against 0.644 for distance alone. We arrived here after measuring three standard architectural responses to occlusion, depth fusion, occlusion-simulating augmentation, and attention, none of which improved detection outside its training distribution in the configurations we tested, and after finding that a detector trained on German roads loses half its accuracy on self-annotated street scenes in Lagos, Nigeria. Signals that need no local annotation are worth more in settings that benchmarks do not represent.

articles.title: Procedural Adversarial Learning
articles.content: For many computer vision tasks, neural networks can be trained to produce a low average error, yet they still fail on seemingly simple scenes. Reducing these failures requires first finding them, but they may not be in a fixed dataset. We study procedural adversarial learning (PAL), a framework of minimax training and adversarial evaluation which searches the input space of a procedural generator for difficult instances. The procedural generator is an interpretable program mapping a low-dimensional vector of control parameters (e.g. layout, lighting, pose) to a rendered image and its label. We introduce the Simple-PAT algorithm, which uses zeroth-order optimization in the procedural generator's parameter space to propose adversarial training samples that are generated on demand. We also create PAL-Dojo, a collection of efficient procedural generators for surface normal estimation, image segmentation, and human pose estimation. Against a cross-model black-box adversary with 50M aggregate queries, Simple-PAT reduces worst-case error by a geometric mean of 3.15x compared to standard training and 2.63x compared to the strongest robust training baseline. Code is available at https://github.com/princeton-vl/procedural-adversarial-learning.

articles.title: Dull, Dirty, Dangerous? Working Conditions and the Limits of Occupational AI Exposure
articles.content: Automation is often justified as relief from dull, dirty, and dangerous work. I examine how these conditions relate to occupational AI exposure using 21 O*NET items across 754 US occupations. Higher exposure is associated with lower condition scores under a large language model (LLM) measure and AI Occupational Exposure (AIOE), with equal occupation weights and employment weights. Adjustment for physical demands, required education, training and experience, and wages reduces the composite association. The adjusted confidence intervals include zero for LLM exposure and remain below zero for AIOE. Separating repetition from restricted discretion also changes what the combined Dull score conveys. These comparisons show how item groupings and occupational characteristics shape the interpretation of exposure estimates. Occupational profiles offer a starting point for selecting contrasting research settings. Establishing desired automation or realized relief requires evidence about workers' preferences and specific interventions.
